summary: How grape skins give red wine its color and tannin, from delicate Pinot Noir to powerful Cabernet Sauvignon.

compareSwitch.title: Merlot and Cabernet, side by side
compareSwitch.intro: Bordeaux's two great grapes. They often blend together: Merlot softens Cabernet's structure, and Cabernet adds backbone to Merlot.

cards.name: Merlot
cards.headline: Soft and plush
cards.footnote: Ripens earlier and has less tannin. Famous on Bordeaux's Right Bank, in Pomerol and Saint-Émilion.

cards.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
cards.headline: Bold and structured
cards.footnote: Thick skins give deep color and firm tannins. Famous on Bordeaux's Left Bank, in Pauillac and Margaux, and in Napa Valley.

flashCards.title: Three more grapes to know
flashCards.intro: Tap a grape. One card each, in the words of this lesson.

cards.name: Syrah
cards.text: The Northern Rhône makes elegant, age-worthy Syrah. Australia's Barossa Valley makes bold, jammy Shiraz.

cards.name: Grenache
cards.text: Thrives in hot, dry climates, giving generous, fruity wines with soft tannins. A key grape in Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

cards.name: Malbec
cards.text: High-altitude vineyards give inky, full-bodied wines with velvety tannins.

scenario.title: Put it to work
scenario.intro: Reading builds knowledge. Choosing builds judgment.
scenario.prompt: A guest tells you: “I would like a red wine, but nothing heavy.” Which bottle do you reach for?

choices.feedback: Pinot Noir is red wine's most delicate grape: lighter in color, with silky tannins and bright red fruit.
Napa Cabernet is powerful and fruit-forward, with firm tannins. That is the heavy style this guest wants to skip. Pinot Noir is the better call.
Mendoza Malbec is inky and full-bodied. Pinot Noir is the better call.

questions.prompt: Where does red wine get its color and tannin?
options: From contact with the grape skins during fermentation
From the juice of the grape
From the yeast used in fermentation
questions.explanation: Contact with the grape skins during fermentation gives red wine its color, its tannin, and much of its flavor.

questions.prompt: Which grape ripens earlier and has less tannin?
questions.explanation: Merlot ripens earlier than Cabernet Sauvignon and has less tannin, which makes it rounder and easier to enjoy young.

questions.prompt: Where has Malbec found its ideal home?
questions.explanation: Mendoza, where high-altitude vineyards make inky, full-bodied Malbec with velvety tannins.

tryThisWeek.title: Three things to try this week
items: Pour a Pinot Noir and a Cabernet Sauvignon side by side and compare the color and the grip of the tannins
Taste a Merlot and look for plum, black cherry, and chocolate
Smell a Syrah and look for black pepper and violet
